name: PhysicalAI-SmartSpaces
description:
Physical AI Smart Spaces Dataset
	



	
		
	
	
		Overview
	

Comprehensive, annotated dataset for multi-camera tracking and 2D/3D object detection. This dataset is synthetically generated with Omniverse and Cosmos Transfer.
This dataset consists of over 280 hours of video from across nearly 1,800 cameras from indoor scenes in warehouses, hospitals, retail, and more. The dataset is time synchronized for tracking humans, forklifts, pallet trucks and Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs)… See the full description on the dataset page: https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/PhysicalAI-SmartSpaces.
rai:dataLimitations: This dataset is limited to synthetic indoor scenes (warehouses, hospitals, retail, labs) captured by statically mounted, pre-calibrated cameras at 1080p/30 FPS H.264; it does not cover outdoor, mobile-camera, low-light, adverse-weather, fish-eye, thermal, or compressed-stream conditions. Appearance is rendered per-view by Cosmos Transfer 2.5, which is single-view rather than multi-view-consistent, so the same object may look subtly different across simultaneous camera views, a future multi-view-capable release will address this. Calibration schemas also differ between MTMC_Tracking_2024 (flat fields) and MTMC_Tracking_2025/2026 (nested sensors[]), and consumers must handle both. The dataset was built as the benchmark for the 8th and 9th AI City Challenges and is not a deployment-readiness proxy. It is not recommended for clinical decision-making, production surveillance, biometric or facial recognition, real-world safety-critical control loops, demographic or fairness studies, outdoor or mobile-camera tracking, or any harm-risk application without explicit sim-to-real validation and human oversight.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is dominated by warehouse environments, with hospital, retail, and lab scenes contributing only a small share, so full-dataset metrics are biased toward warehouse-style geometry, lighting, and traffic patterns. Human characters are synthetic avatars from a finite Omniverse asset library, introducing demographic bias toward the appearances chosen by the library's authors; age, body type, skin tone, clothing, mobility aids, and gait are neither balanced nor labeled, and the dataset must not be used for fairness claims across demographic groups. Camera viewpoints follow industrial CCTV conventions (overhead and oblique), under-representing eye-level, body-worn, vehicle-mounted, and fish-eye perspectives. Appearance is rendered by Cosmos Transfer 2.5, which inherits the geographic, lighting, and demographic biases of its own training data and propagates them into the synthetic frames.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation:
The publicly released portions of this dataset (MTMC_Tracking_2024, MTMC_Tracking_2025, and the MTMC_Tracking_2026 train/val splits) contain no personal or sensitive information: all scenes, characters, depth maps, and annotations are synthetically generated in NVIDIA Omniverse / Isaac Sim, with no real human subjects, no real biometric or facial data, and no real-world location, audio, or text content. None of the categories listed (gender, age, geography, language, culture, socio-economic status, health/medical data, political/religious beliefs) are present in these splits. The "Hospital" scenes are simulated environments and contain no patient information.

The 2026 release additionally references a hidden real-world evaluation target captured by NVIDIA in real smart-space environments. Every individual appearing in this real footage has provided a signed, written consent agreement authorizing the capture target, no person appears in the real data without explicit individual consent on file with NVIDIA. Because the target depicts real people in identifiable settings, it implicitly contains the categories of gender, age, and geographic location of capture; no health/medical, political/religious, socio-economic, language, or culture annotations are recorded. The hidden target is treated as an evaluation-only resource: raw video is not publicly redistributed, access is mediated solely through the AI City Challenge online evaluation server, manual labeling of the test set by participants is prohibited by the challenge rules, and the target is excluded from training use. These access controls are the primary privacy-preserving measure. Residual risk is limited to the small population of individuals captured in the real footage and is mitigated by withholding the raw frames from public release. The dataset, including the hidden target, is not authorized for use in biometric, facial recognition, demographic profiling, or surveillance systems targeting real individuals.
rai:dataUseCases: This dataset is intended to measure multi-camera 3D perception in indoor smart spaces, including joint detection, 3D localization, and identity association across synchronized overlapping and non-overlapping camera networks. Validity has been established across three rounds of public benchmarking on the AI City Challenge evaluation server (2024 person-only 3D location tracking, 2025 and 2026 multi-class 3D box tracking), using 3D Higher Order Tracking Accuracy (HOTA), with leaderboard evidence from 7 ranked teams in 2024 (HOTA 40.34–71.94) and 4 ranked teams in 2025 (HOTA 25.40–69.91). Utility for synthetic-to-real transfer is being directly measured through the hidden 2026 real-world target.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive impact: advances reproducible research on multi-camera 3D perception in indoor smart spaces (warehouse, hospital, retail, lab), supporting applications such as human–robot collision avoidance, logistics safety, and Sim2Real generalization research, while reducing the need to collect or redistribute real-person video by substituting synthetic supervision. Risks: repurposing for workplace and labor surveillance, public-space monitoring, biometric re-identification, or facial recognition that disproportionately affects workers, patients, customers, and other vulnerable populations in the depicted settings; over-reliance on synthetic-benchmark scores as a proxy for deployment readiness; and bias propagation from Cosmos Transfer 2.5's training data and the finite Omniverse avatar library, which may cause underperformance on underrepresented body types, skin tones, mobility aids, and gait patterns. Mitigation: the public training and validation release is fully synthetic with no real-person imagery; the 2026 real-world Sim2Real target is held out behind the AI City Challenge evaluation server with manual test-set labeling prohibited and training on the target excluded; the server enforces auditable scoring and requires code release from award-eligible teams; and this dataset card and the accompanying paper document the limitations, biases, and out-of-scope uses (including clinical decision-making, production surveillance, biometric or facial recognition, safety-critical control loops, and demographic fairness studies) for which the dataset is explicitly not recommended.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac Sim Applications
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: The data is collected with NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac Sim. The 2025 and 2026 components use IsaacSim Replicator Agent (IRA), IsaacSim Replicator Object (IRO), IsaacSim.Anim.Robot (IAR),  isaacsim.sensors.rtx.placement (ISRP), and isaacsim.sensors.rtx.calibration (ISRC) style pipelines to configure mobile agents, place scene objects, render synchronized camera streams, and produce corresponding labels/annotations in a consistent world coordinate system.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac Sim Applications
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: All annotations were generated by using all components mentioned in data collection.
